newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iraqi oil flow from Mina Bakr delayed by metre.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi oil flow from Mina Bakr delayed by metre.

text.p: Iraqi oil flow from the southern port of Mina al-Bakr is expected later this week after a new Malaysian-made metre is installed, regional shipping sources said on Tuesday.

"The metre has just arrived in the Jordanian capital Amman on a Royal Jordanian flight after a 36-hour delay because of technical failure to the aircraft in Singapore airport," one source told Reuters.
"The 500-kg metre is expected to leave Amman for Baghdad later today (Tuesday) and we hope it will be operational by Thursday at the earliest, after which oil pumping could commence," he added.
"The Iraqis are fuming with anger over this delay".
Iraq's Oil Minister Amir Muhammed Rasheed said in a statement that oil would start to flow from the southern Iraqi terminal on Friday or Saturday.
The capacity of Iraq to export oil directly from Mina al-Bakr will not be known until the first oil is pushed through the system, a spokesman for inspectors Saybolt said earlier.
A functional test can only be done once a tanker arrives at the port because it has no storage tanks, he added.
Pipeline oil flows into storage tanks have already been tested at the Iraqi-Turkish border and at Turkey's Meditteranean terminal at Ceyhan.
Earlier, oil sources in Asia said Iraqi crude was unlikely to hit Asia until January due to problems at Mina al-Bakr, including rusted and corroded pipelines.
